assessments.reasoning: Section 5.9 gives Boolean operands and explicitly makes conjunction's right operand conditional on an evaluated true left operand and disjunction's on an evaluated false one. A valid expression's result in the complementary cases requires the right Boolean value.

challenge.method: Enumerate both left Boolean values for each operator and contrast exclusive-or and vector operations. Use a legal right operand able to return either truth value and have an observable language-level effect.
challenge.results: From the source rule, conjunction short-circuits only on false and disjunction only on true. When the left value alone does not determine the result, the right value is required. Exclusive-or evaluates both, and the vector built-ins do not extend the scalar binary rule to vector operands.

limitations: The proposition is the language's abstract evaluation rule for valid scalar Boolean operands with normal left evaluation. It does not prescribe instructions emitted by an optimizer.
